objective: Quantify and statistically test differences in blood glucose levels across three patient cohorts (Diabetes, Stroke, CKD) restricted to ages 30-70 with valid (non-zero, non-missing) glucose; report Kruskal-Wallis H result and, if significant, Dunn post-hoc pairwise comparisons with Bonferroni correction.

input_data.unit_compatibility: All three glucose fields are mg/dL -> directly poolable without rescaling.

harmonization_spec.arff_parsing: Parse @data block manually; treat '?' as NaN; drop blank fields from rows with malformed field counts (1 such row, age/bgr unaffected).
harmonization_spec.reference_artifact: harmonized_glucose_filtered.csv already exists upstream (4464 rows) and should be consumed as-is / re-verified, not regenerated with different rules.

filtering_rules.glucose: drop rows where glucose is 0 or missing/NaN
filtering_rules.application_order: convert -> coerce numeric (errors='coerce') -> drop NaN age/glucose -> apply age window -> drop glucose <= 0

data_qc_checks: row counts per source match expected_shapes above (Diabetes 1306, Stroke 2885, CKD 273)
no NaN and no <=0 values in glucose after filtering
glucose dtypes numeric; source only takes the three allowed labels
CKD filter drop = 400 - 90(out of age) - 44(missing bgr) - overlaps -> expect 273

overall_test.name: Kruskal-Wallis
overall_test.rationale: Non-parametric 3-group comparison; glucose distributions are right-skewed and heteroscedastic, so ANOVA assumptions do not hold.
overall_test.decision_rule: if p < 0.05 proceed to post-hoc; record statistic (H) and p_value

posthoc.name: Dunn post-hoc
posthoc.implementation: Dunn (1964) z statistic on pooled ranks (scipy.stats.rankdata with average ties), per-group tie correction; z = (mean_rank_i - mean_rank_j)/sqrt((N(N+1)/12 - ties/(12(N-1))) * (1/n_i + 1/n_j))
posthoc.reported_p_value: Bonferroni-adjusted p in output.csv p_value column; 'significant' flag = p_adj < 0.05
posthoc.contingency: Skipped entirely if Kruskal-Wallis p >= 0.05 (unlikely per upstream run)

output.csv.formatting: significant serialized as literal True/False; float statistics/p-values full precision, no rounding to 0

output.png.annotation: Kruskal-Wallis p-value text on figure (scientific notation), plus title/legend/axis labels; axis label 'Blood Glucose (mg/dL)', x-limits clipped to pooled 0.5-99.5 percentile for readability, dpi>=150

validation_checks: output.csv has exactly 4 data rows with the 5 required columns and exact label strings
3 pairwise rows + 1 overall row; significant column values in {True, False}
output.png exists, >20KB, non-blank, three distinct colored series rendered
results reproducible: re-run yields identical statistic/p_value (no randomness involved)
narrative conclusions (which cohort has highest median glucose) must match observed_group_profile_for_sanity_check, not be invented
risks_and_notes: CKD 'bgr' is a random (non-fasting) glucose reading while Diabetes 'Glucose' is a 2h OGTT plasma value and Stroke 'avg_glucose_level' is a long-run average; unit harmonization is exact (mg/dL) but measurement semantics differ -> significant differences partly reflect measurement protocol, must be stated as a limitation.
Stroke cohort dominates sample size (2885/4464, 65%); with such large N tiny differences become significant, so effect sizes / median differences should accompany p-values.
Diabetes glucose capped at 199 in source data (truncation), which compresses its upper tail and can bias the test.
Zero glucose in the Diabetes file are missing-value placeholders, not true zeros -> excluding them is required, not optional.
